subject: system
statement: Developers build by opening the Visual Studio solution in Release mode, with version.bat stamping the git version into a source file. Separately, the GitHub workflow .github/workflows/latest.yml (a file left out of the read, so not cited here) runs on every push to master (and on demand): it stamps the version, builds Release with MSBuild on a Windows server, prints the executable's hash (never compared to anything) and uploads the unsigned Policy Plus.exe to an Amazon S3 bucket as PolicyPlusLatest.exe, using stored AWS secrets through a third-party action (stcalica/s3-upload@0.0.1) and the old actions/checkout@v2. That bucket copy is what is distributed as the latest build. No test step exists.

evidence.shows: Manual developer build in Visual Studio.
Writes the git description into a version source file.

statement: The program's manifest (a left-out file) asks it to run with the highest rights the signed-in user has. Access to policy data is decided by Windows, not by the program. When an administrator downloads policy files, the program enables ownership and restore privileges to take control of the destination folder.

evidence.shows: Takes ownership of destination when running as administrator.
Enables a named Windows privilege for the process.

statement: We go with the program running only on Windows desktops used by administrators, as a single copy started by a person, from a downloaded executable. No installer, service or schedule exists in the code.

assumed.why: No file states the intended audience or deployment; the code only shows a Windows executable.
assumed.ifWrong: If it must run on servers, unattended or on other operating systems, parts of the design would need to change.

evidence.shows: Output type is a Windows executable.
